value.body: An ANM (Auxiliary Nurse Midwife) is the frontline health worker for a group of villages or an urban ward. Most work at government sub-health centres and Ayushman Arogya Mandirs; private hospitals and NGOs also hire them. A day includes immunisation sessions, check-ups for pregnant women and new mothers, home visits with ASHA workers and entering records in health registers and apps.

items.label: Typical entry
items.note: Registration with the State Nursing Council is required

items.label: Where the work is
items.value: Sub-health centres, primary health centres, private hospitals and NGOs

items.label: Sub-health centres
items.note: The norm is at least one ANM per sub-centre
items.source: MoHFW, Health Dynamics of India (Infrastructure & Human Resources) 2022-23 (as reported)

items.label: ANMs on nursing council registers
items.note: Older figure; registers include people no longer working
items.source: MoHFW Lok Sabha reply citing Indian Nursing Council (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Complete the ANM diploma at an INC-recognised nursing school and register with the State Nursing Council. Then apply to state health department or National Health Mission recruitment, or to private hospitals and NGO health projects.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Working with ASHA and Anganwadi workers

value.title: At a glance
items: Many government posts are NHM contracts with rural postings.
Some states promote ANMs to Lady Health Visitor or health supervisor.
Many ANMs later study GNM or B.Sc Nursing to move into hospital nursing.

competition.note: GNM / ANM graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
